memory_versions.text:
Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles are approved and available: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- Do not change strategy based on isolated unsubscribes; two support-reported unsubscribes provided insufficient evidence.
- Audience/list growth and absence of deliverability complaints do not identify a winning angle.
- Results are delayed and aggregated (“last 2 pushes”), with no per-day breakdown. Avoid attributing aggregate outcomes to a specific send.
- Quality story (B) has produced positive partial results in aggregate: reported outcomes include 1/2 and 1/2 landed. It is a credible, low-pressure default.
- Customer testimonial (D) also has positive aggregate evidence: one report of 2/2 landed, though attribution is uncertain.
- Limited-time urgency (C) had a 2/2 aggregate result once, but this is too little evidence to conclude it is superior.
- No meaningful evidence yet supports or rejects price cuts (A).
- Continue testing B, C, and D rather than overfitting to sparse reports; use B as the safest default when no stronger signal exists. Track sends and outcomes by day if possible.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- Recent practice heavily favored B (quality story), but analytics repeatedly reported 0 of the last 2 pushes landed. Because results are delayed, aggregated, and lack per-day/angle attribution, this does not prove B caused the misses; it does weaken the case for treating B as the automatic default.
- Earlier aggregate evidence for B (1/2 and 1/2 landed) is now mixed with several recent 0/2 reports. Treat B as viable but unconfirmed, not the safest unquestioned choice.
- D has one positive aggregate report (2/2 landed), though attribution is uncertain. C also had one 2/2 result, insufficient to establish superiority.
- A still has no meaningful performance evidence.
- Do not change strategy based on isolated support-reported unsubscribes. List growth and lack of deliverability complaints are not evidence of a winning angle.
- Stop repeatedly selecting B without learning. Rotate B, C, D, and A where feasible; prioritize C/D for upcoming tests to obtain comparative evidence, while retaining B as one test arm.
- Track each send, angle, date, and outcome separately. Until reporting improves, avoid attributing any “last 2 pushes” result to a specific send or angle.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- B is viable but unconfirmed. Earlier aggregate results (1/2 and 1/2) are mixed with recent 0/2 reports; do not treat B as the automatic default.
- D has one positive aggregate report (2/2), and C previously had one 2/2 result, but attribution is uncertain. New C-heavy activity produced pooled reports of 0/2, 2/2, 1/2, 1/2, and 0/2. These do not establish C’s performance because reports lack per-send/per-day attribution and include queued sends.
- Recent practice overused C rather than rotating angles, so do not continue selecting C by default. Use D, A, and B in upcoming tests, with C only as part of a balanced rotation.
- A still lacks meaningful performance evidence and should be tested rather than inferred to be weak.
- Record every send separately with date, angle, and outcome. Treat queued results as pending; never map a later pooled “last 2 pushes” report to a specific send or angle.
- Legal approval for all four angles and refreshed creative permit testing but do not prove effectiveness.
- No deliverability complaints and modest list growth are operational signals only, not evidence that any angle wins. Ignore isolated support-reported unsubscribes when changing strategy.
- Avoid repeated selection without learning. Seek comparable evidence across all four angles before declaring a winner.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- B remains viable but unconfirmed; do not use it as the automatic default.
- D has an earlier positive aggregate report (2/2), and C had one 2/2 report, but attribution is uncertain. Recent pooled reports (0/2, 2/2, 1/2, 1/2, 0/2, plus later 0/2 results) cannot establish angle performance because they lack per-send/per-day attribution and include queued sends.
- Recent activity heavily overused A as well as previously overusing C. A now has many recorded selections, but no attributable performance evidence; do not infer that it is weak or strong. Upcoming tests should rotate D, B, A, and C rather than defaulting to any one angle.
- Recent send log: Day 31 A queued; Day 32 A with pooled 1/2; Day 33 D queued (despite conflicting narrative text); Day 34 A with pooled 2/2; Days 35–38 A, with queued/p pooled 0/2 reports; Day 39 D queued (not A); Day 40 A with pooled 0/2. Treat all pooled outcomes as unattributed and queued outcomes as pending.
- Record each send separately with date, angle, and outcome. Resolve discrepancies using the explicit ANGLE field, not narrative commentary; never map “last 2 pushes” to a specific send.
- Legal approval and refreshed creative permit testing but do not prove effectiveness.
- Deliverability complaints, list growth, and isolated support-reported unsubscribes are operational signals only.
- Seek comparable, attributable evidence across all four angles before declaring a winner.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- No angle is proven superior. B remains viable but unconfirmed; D has some positive aggregate history, but attribution is uncertain. Do not default to either.
- Recent pooled reports (including 0/2, 1/2, and 2/2) lack per-day/per-send attribution and may include queued sends. Treat them as unattributed; queued outcomes remain pending.
- Days 41–50 log:
  - 41 B queued
  - 42 B, pooled 0/2
  - 43 D queued
  - 44 B, pooled 1/2
  - 45 D queued
  - 46 B, pooled 0/2
  - 47 B queued
  - 48 D, pooled 1/2
  - 49 D queued
  - 50 B, pooled 2/2
  These results do not establish B or D performance.
- A has been heavily used previously without attributable evidence; C was also previously overused. Do not infer either is weak or strong. Upcoming tests should deliberately rotate A, B, C, and D and seek comparable attributable samples.
- Record every send separately with date, explicit ANGLE field, and outcome. Resolve conflicts using ANGLE, not narrative text. Never assign “last 2 pushes” to a specific send.
- Legal approval and refreshed creative permit testing but do not demonstrate effectiveness.
- Deliverability complaints, list growth, and isolated support-reported unsubscribes are operational signals only.
- Continue collecting per-send/per-day results across all four angles before declaring a winner.

Campaign angle notes:

- Four angles remain approved: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial.
- No angle is proven superior. B remains viable but unconfirmed; D has positive aggregate history, but attribution is uncertain. Do not default to either.
- Pooled analytics reports (0/2, 1/2, 2/2) lack per-day/per-send attribution and may include queued sends. Treat them as unattributed; queued outcomes remain pending. Never assign “last 2 pushes” to a specific send.
- Days 41–50: B/D were sent or queued, with pooled 0/2, 1/2, 0/2, 1/2, and 2/2 reports. These do not establish B or D performance.
- Days 51–60: A was used every day. Sends were queued on 51, 53, 55, 57, and 59; pooled reports on 52 (0/2), 54 (1/2), 56 (1/2), 58 (0/2), and 60 (0/2). These results are also unattributed and do not establish A performance.
- A and C have been heavily used historically; recent A concentration creates imbalance but is not evidence that A is weak or strong. Resume deliberate rotation across A, B, C, and D, prioritizing fresh, comparable, attributable samples—especially B, C, and D after the A-heavy run.
- Record every send separately with date, explicit ANGLE field, queue status, and outcome. Resolve conflicts using ANGLE, not narrative text.
- Legal approval, refreshed creative, deliverability, list growth, and support-reported unsubscribes are operational signals only, not effectiveness evidence.
- Continue per-send/per-day measurement across all four angles before declaring a winner.
